title: Sulfur Dioxide — Overview (Public edition)
description: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) is a bent, pungent gas released by volcanoes and by burning sulfur-containing fuels; in the atmosphere it oxidizes to sulfuric acid, driving acid rain. It is also a food preservative (E220) and the gateway to sulfuric acid manufacture.
how_it_works: Read top-down: identity first, then structure, properties, reactions, and the deterministic scale chain. Each record derives from the molecule's parsed composition.

title: Sulfur Dioxide — Identity and Composition
description: Sulfur Dioxide is identified by the molecule SO2: SO2. Parsed deterministically, it contains O2 + S — 3 molecule(s), 32 protons and 32 electrons per molecule, molar mass 64.058 g/mol.
how_it_works: The build-time formula parser tokenizes the formula (handling parentheses and multipliers), looks up CIAAW 2021 atomic weights, and sums mass, atom, proton, and electron counts. The embedded demo re-derives the same numbers in JavaScript and fails the build if they differ.

title: Sulfur Dioxide — Structure and Bonding
description: Bent, O-S-O angle about 119 degrees, S-O bond about 1.43 A. Polar; the sulfur lone pair makes it a good ligand and reductant.
how_it_works: Structure determines properties: geometry sets polarity, polarity sets solubility and boiling point, bonding sets reactivity. Read this record before the properties records.
